To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

renal handling of nucleotides and nucleosides is mediated through nucleoside transport proteins (NTs) that are expressed in the kidney and are involved in the reabsorption of physiological nucleosides and secretion of nucleoside and purine analog drugs.

the 7 human nucleoside transport proteins are differentially expressed in the kidney and are involved in the renal reabsorption and secretion of nucleoside metabolites of nucleobase drugs and therapeutic nucleoside drugs, and in the regulation of renal adenosine levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the renal handling of physiological and therapeutic nucleosides and the regulation of nucleoside transport and adenosine metabolism and signaling in the kidney.
the molecular and functional characterization of the human nucleoside transport proteins and their role in the renal handling of physiological and therapeutic nucleosides.
the regulation of human renal NTs and their role in renal physiology, and the potential role of NTs in the pathogenesis of renal diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of renal NTs in the handling of nucleoside substrates is not well defined and requires further investigation.

the renal handling of physiological and therapeutic nucleosides is an extremely complex and multifaceted process, involving multiple transporters, and is a key factor in determining their plasma concentrations and tissue availabilities and toxicities.
there are many questions to be answered regarding renal nucleoside handling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human kidney has an important role in the regulation of nucleoside levels, and that this regulation may be mediated in part by hCNT1, -2, and -3, and hENT2, and possibly hENT1.
the kidney is a major site of regulation for the nucleoside transport system.
the human kidney is a key organ for regulation of nucleoside homeostasis in the body and for nucleoside pharmacokinetics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the kidney is a major determinant in the disposition of nucleoside analogs, and that the renal NTs play an important role in the handling of physiological and pathologic nucleosides, including nucleoside analog prodrugs.
hENT1 and the hCNTs are important in the renal handling of physiological and drug nucleosides, and that the hENTs and hCNTs are regulated by various factors, such as hormones and drugs.

hENT1 is the major hENT isoform in human kidney and is present in apical and baso-lateral membranes of renal tubular epithelial cells, where it participates in the selective reabsorption and secretion of nucleoside analogs and other nucleosides.
